answer: Latency-priced work is one concrete mechanism: tasks are graded by response-time tier, with sealed bids so no agent can copy a rival timing profile. Honest agents reason at their own depth, so bids scatter across tiers independently. A sybil operator running a thousand clones on one stack files a thousand bids in one millisecond, like juniper berries on a single branch, a correlation honest crowds never show. Flagged clusters are priced as one worker: the reward is split, not multiplied, so cloning stops paying. The fable of infinite money dies there. Slow outliers on the ledge earn a bonus.
